**New Findings**

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33  
DESCRIPTION: Non-finite fingerprint values are not rejected, and `NaN` can be turned into an artificially strong capability signal. At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L410), `_compute_pool_max()` uses `np.max`, so any `NaN` in a pool dimension contaminates that dimension’s max. At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L302), `np.where(pool_max > 0, raw / pool_max, 0.0)` treats `NaN > 0` as false and replaces the normalized value with `0.0`; then [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L304) inverts `D_decay` to `1.0`. I verified this with a direct runtime reproduction: a model with `CapabilityFingerprint(float('nan'), 0.8, 0.9, 0.7)` received PM/COL/PAR scores of `1.0` and won PM instead of failing fast.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `CapabilityFingerprint.__post_init__` validation for finiteness and valid ranges, reject `NaN`/`inf` before scoring, and assert that `_capability_score()` returns a finite value. If `NaN` must be tolerated, define explicit semantics and use `np.nanmax` plus per-dimension handling rather than the current implicit promotion.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: The live-fingerprint reassignment fix is not stateful. At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L543), `reassign()` builds a temporary `models_for_scoring` list from `live_fingerprints`, but it never writes those updated fingerprints back into [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L399) `_models` or any internal live cache. A later `reassign()` call without `live_fingerprints` silently falls back to the original fingerprints. I verified this directly: one `reassign(..., live_fingerprints=...)` moved COL from `m2` to `m3`, and the next plain `reassign()` moved COL back to `m2`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Persist the latest fingerprints inside `RoleAssignment` after reassignment, or make `live_fingerprints` mandatory once adaptive mode is enabled. The current optional side-channel API is too easy to use incorrectly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` advertises round-based failure history but does not actually use the round index. The parameter appears at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L518) and is documented at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L528), but the penalty calculation at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L580) only averages an append-only event list populated by [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L621). That means the implementation tracks “number of `record_failure()` calls” rather than “failure status by round.” I verified this with a direct reproduction: calling `record_failure("m2", True)` and then `record_failure("m2", False)` before `reassign(1)` produced a history rate of `0.5` and changed the role outcome, even though both writes could belong to the same round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store failure status keyed by `round_idx`, or maintain a fixed round-aligned structure and compute `phi_hist` only from rounds `< round_idx`. If duplicate writes occur for the same round, reject or overwrite them instead of averaging them as separate events.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: The low-signal fallback for degenerate fingerprints is configured and documented, but not implemented anywhere. The safeguard is declared at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L185) as `fingerprint_min_signal`, and the project documentation states at [EXPERIMENTAL_RESULTS.md](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/EXPERIMENTAL_RESULTS.md#L858) that when all models fall below this threshold the system should switch to round-robin assignment. A repo-wide search shows no reads of `fingerprint_min_signal`, so Role Assignment still performs score-based argmax/tiebreak selection in exactly the degenerate regime this safeguard was meant to cover.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement an explicit low-signal check in `assign()` and `reassign()` or in `DynamicManager` before role selection. When all active fingerprints are below threshold, use a deterministic fallback such as round-robin or “keep current roles unless invalid,” and add tests for the collapse case.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R7_F015  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `theta_col` is a dead public configuration parameter. It is declared at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L104) as a COL threshold, but neither `assign()` nor `reassign()` consult it anywhere in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L445) or [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L516). I verified this directly: setting `DynamicManagementConfig(theta_col=0.99)` still assigned a COL by plain argmax. Callers who set this field get silently ignored behavior rather than thresholded COL selection.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement threshold gating for COL assignment in both initial assignment and reassignment, or remove `theta_col` from the public config until that behavior exists. Silent no-op configuration is misleading.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Residual note: `pytest` could not run in this sandbox because there is no writable temp directory, so verification here is from direct code inspection plus targeted `python3 -c` reproductions.
